definition: LipNet is a deep neural network for audio-visual speech recognition (ASVR).
details: It was created by University of Oxford researchers Yannis Assael, Brendan Shillingford, Shimon Whiteson, and Nando de Freitas. The researchers stated that could match mouth movements to text with 93 percent accuracy, though it was criticized for its test using a limited dataset of words and grammar. It was used in Nvidia's autonomous "backseat driver" prototype Co-Pilot.

explainer.lead: LipNet is a deep neural network for audio-visual speech recognition. It matters as an early demonstration of matching mouth movements to text, and it was used in an Nvidia autonomous driving prototype.

tiers.eli5: It is a program that reads lips on video and writes down what is being said, like a very fast lipreader.
tiers.practitioner: The model maps video of mouth movements to text and can serve as a visual component in recognition systems. A known pitfall is that headline accuracy can reflect a limited dataset of words and grammar, so results may not generalize.
tiers.paperLevel: LipNet is a deep neural network for audio-visual speech recognition, created by Yannis Assael, Brendan Shillingford, Shimon Whiteson, and Nando de Freitas at the University of Oxford; the researchers stated it could match mouth movements to text with 93 percent accuracy, though it was criticized for testing on a limited dataset of words and grammar.

explainer.example: Given silent video of a speaker, LipNet outputs the corresponding text transcript of the spoken words.
